also: at the foot of the mountain
at the foot of the hill

terms.grammar: rādīx, rādīcis f., with the genitive; often plural rādīcēs
evidence: Caes. BG 7.36: sub ipsīs rādīcibus montis (Lewis & Short s.v. rādīx)
Cic. Tusc. 2.52: in rādīcibus Caucasī nātus (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: Domus avī sub colle est; inde ascendēmus.
phrases.english: Grandpa’s house is at the foot of the hill; from there we’ll climb up.

phrases.latin: Danda opera ut potissimum sub rādīcibus montis silvestris vīllam pōnat
phrases.english: one should try, above all, to put the farmhouse at the foot of a wooded hill

phrases.latin: hostēs sub monte cōnsēdisse mīlia passuum ab ipsīus castrīs octō
phrases.english: that the enemy had encamped at the foot of the hill, eight miles from his camp

phrases.latin: Vīlla in colle īmō sita prōspicit quasi ex summō
phrases.english: the house stands at the foot of a hill, yet looks out as if from the top

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency.
Lewis & Short: radix
